title: Certainty ladder: 〜かもしれない / 〜はず / でしょう-deepen

grammarPoints.rule: かもしれない means 'might be' — a guess you are genuinely not sure about. Attach it to the plain form of what you are guessing: a verb or い-adjective in dictionary form as-is, but a noun or な-adjective DROPS its だ first — がくせいかもしれない, 'might be a student,' never がくせいだかもしれない. あめが ふるかもしれない, 'it might rain.' Casual speech often shortens this to bare かも at a sentence end, but that shortcut is not a separate word — it is か plus the も you already know, worn down by speed, and this course never registers it as its own atom. Compare でしょう, which you already own: でしょう states a fairly confident guess out loud; かもしれない admits real uncertainty, often even to yourself.

antiPattern.ja: がくせいだかもしれない。
antiPattern.why: Noun and な-adjective hosts DROP だ before かもしれない — がくせいかもしれない, 'might be a student.' Keeping だ borrows でしょう's own different pattern by mistake.

grammarPoints.rule: はず means 'should be' — not a guess but a confident conclusion, because you have a real reason. A plain verb or い-adjective attaches straight to はず: くるはずだ, 'he should be coming' (I know his schedule). A noun needs の first: がくせいのはずだ, 'she should be a student' (I saw her ID). A な-adjective needs な first: げんきなはずだ, 'she should be fine' (I just talked to her). This is the opposite move from かもしれない, which DROPS だ for the same two hosts — はず INSERTS の or な instead. Compare でしょう: でしょう is a guess said out loud; はず claims real evidence backs the conclusion.

examples.ja: やくそくが あるから、くるはずだ。
examples.en: Since there's a promise, he should be coming.

antiPattern.why: A noun host needs の before はず, not だ — がくせいのはずだ, 'she should be a student.' だ belongs to かもしれない's opposite rule, not this one.

grammarPoints.rule: Two extra shapes push はず further, both riding the same の/な/bare connector rule as before. はずだった says something SHOULD have happened, by your own evidence, but you don't yet know if it did — くるはずだったが、まだ こない, 'he was supposed to come, but he still hasn't.' はずがない flips はず into a flat denial, 'there's no way' — げんきなはずが ない, 'there's no way she's fine' (the evidence points the other way entirely).

antiPattern.ja: くるはずだが、まだ こない。
antiPattern.why: Reporting a broken expectation about something that already should have happened needs the past はずだった, not plain はずだ — くるはずだったが、まだ こない, 'he was supposed to come, but hasn't yet.'

grammarPoints.rule: Four ways to guess, one ladder of how sure you sound. にちがいない sits at the top — 'must be,' near-certainty from strong evidence (you'll only ever hear this one, never build it). はず comes next — 'should be,' a confident conclusion backed by a real reason. でしょう and its casual twin だろう sit in the middle — a fair, everyday guess, said out loud (だろう also stays recognition-only). かもしれない sits at the bottom — 'might be,' genuine uncertainty, the weakest claim of the four. One test sorts them: finish 'because ~' after the guess. はず and にちがいない always survive that test — you have a real reason. でしょう often has one but doesn't have to say it. かもしれない frequently has none at all — when you DO have a concrete reason, reach up the ladder instead of underselling it.

examples.en: It might fail, but for sure it should succeed.

antiPattern.ja: やくそくが あるから、くるかもしれない。
antiPattern.why: When you actually have a concrete reason — a promise — reach for はず, the evidence-backed rung: やくそくが あるから、くるはずだ. かもしれない undersells real evidence down to a bare guess; save it for when you truly have no reason at all.

beats.stem: やくそくが あるから、たなかさんは くる
beats.tail: 。もしかしたら こないかもしれないけど。
beats.en: Since there's a promise, Tanaka should come. Although maybe he won't.
beats.explanation: はずだ fits the concrete evidence just given — the promise. でしょう would undersell that evidence into a vaguer guess, and かもしれない already covers the weaker possibility in the second clause on its own.

beats.audio: たなかさんは ぜったい せいこうするにちがいない。
beats.answer: Tanaka will absolutely succeed, no doubt.
distractors: Nobody has an opinion about Tanaka.

beats.audio: たなかさんは くるはずだが、こないかもしれない。
beats.answer: Tanaka should come, but he might not.
distractors: Nobody knows anything about Tanaka's plans.

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: たなかさん、くるかな。
lines.en: I wonder if Tanaka is coming.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: やくそくが あるから、くるはずだよ。でも、もしかしたら こないかもしれない。
lines.en: Since there's a promise, he should be coming. But perhaps he might not.

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: たしかに。でも、きっと くるでしょう。
lines.en: True. But surely he'll probably come.

lessons.title: Challenge — the whole certainty ladder, one conversation
lessons.focus: Every rung of the ladder in one arc — かもしれない, はず, でしょう-deepen, and the certainty-ladder synthesis — combined with prior N4 grammar, no new vocabulary

beats.ja: テストは むずかしいでしょうが、じゅぎょうが あったので、せいこうするはずだ。
beats.en: The test is probably hard, but since there was class, it should succeed.

beats.ja: やくそくが あるのに、たなかさんは くるかもしれないし、こないかもしれない。
beats.en: Even though there's a promise, Tanaka might come, and he might not come.

beats.stem: やくそくが あるから、たなかさんは くる
beats.tail: 。もしかしたら こないかもしれないけど。
beats.en: Since there's a promise, Tanaka should come. Although maybe he won't.
beats.explanation: はずだ fits the concrete evidence — the promise — best of the three; でしょう would undersell that evidence into a vaguer guess, and かもしれない already covers the weaker possibility in the second clause on its own.

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ja: テストの けっか、きっと せいこうするにちがいないよ。
lines.en: The test result, surely it'll succeed, no doubt.

lines.speaker: Ken
lines.ja: たぶん だいじょうぶだろう。でも、やくそくが あるから、たなかさんが くるはずだと おもう。
lines.en: Probably it'll be fine. But since there's a promise, I think Tanaka should be coming.

lines.speaker: Mika
lines.ja: うん、もしかしたら ちょっと おくれるかもしれないけど、ぜったい くるでしょう。
lines.en: Yeah, perhaps he might be a little late, but surely he'll probably definitely come.

questions.q: According to the conversation, who sounds MOST certain that things will go well?
options: Tanaka, using にちがいない
Mika, using かもしれない
questions.answer: Tanaka, using にちがいない

beats.ja: テストは むずかしいでしょうが、やくそくが あるから、たなかさんは くるはずだと おもうし、しっぱいするかもしれないとは おもわない。
beats.en: The test is probably hard, but since there's a promise, I think Tanaka should come, and what's more I don't think it might fail.
